data.title: Subpackage Loading
data.tagline: A mechanism that separates mini program code into a main package and subpackages loaded when needed
data.learningOutcome: Separate downloading a code package from loading business data, and identify what must load first.
data.description: A shop’s home screen can live in the main package while its return and repair pages live in a support subpackage. Entering support can then load that package. Downloading page code is separate from fetching order data.

learning.assumes: You have waited for a mini program to open a page.
learning.outcome: Separate downloading a code package from loading business data, and identify what must load first.

distinctions.label: Data request
distinctions.explanation: Retrieves order records or other business data. A subpackage contains the code and resources used to display and operate pages.

distinctions.label: File compression
distinctions.explanation: Reduces file size; subpackaging changes which code is needed at each stage. It does not remove the other code.

explanation.title: Keep the entry and shared resources in the main package
explanation.text: The entry screen and resources needed across ordinary subpackages remain available from the main package. A feature’s pages and private resources can move together.

explanation.title: Load according to the feature being opened
explanation.text: Opening a page in a subpackage can trigger its download. Preloading and caching can change the actual timing; inspect download records rather than assuming it.

data.boundary: Subpackaging does not speed up slow API requests or reduce total code by itself. Size limits and independent-subpackage rules vary by platform and should be checked in the current documentation.

lessonPractice.title: Support pages moved to a subpackage, while the home screen and shared components stayed in the main package. No preload or cache is present. What loads on the first home-only visit?

options.label: The main package; support waits until that feature is opened
options.feedback: The home screen does not need this support package under the stated conditions.

options.label: Only order data; page code stays on the server
options.feedback: The runtime needs the main package’s page code before it can run.

options.label: The main and support packages together as before
options.feedback: Ordinary subpackaging avoids requiring this feature code at first entry when it is not used.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect this WeChat mini program’s packages. Move rarely used return and repair pages into a support subpackage, keeping the entry and shared resources in the main package. Explain which pages moved. Without cached packages, verify the first home visit loads main, support loads on entry, and pages and order data still work.
